title: Generic Protocol for Optimization of Heterologous Protein Production Using Automated Microbioreactor Technology
protocol: Conceive the study and define the methods.
Define the optimization objective based on relevance and practical considerations such as stability, analytical quantification effort, and cultivation time.
Choose a specific time point for optimization, such as 17 hours of cultivation for GFP titer in this study.
Consider alternative objectives like biomass or space-time-yield if applicable.
Optimize parameters rationally and experience-drivenly to reduce the search space.
Select media components for optimization based on expert knowledge and literature data.
Fix glucose concentration at 10 g/L in CgXII medium.
Fix MOPS concentration at 42 g/L in CgXII medium.
Check pH of the medium composition where all stock solutions are added at their maximum and minimum volumes.
Fix KH2PO4 concentration at 1 g/L in CgXII medium.
Fix K2HPO4 concentration at 1 g/L in CgXII medium.
Fix urea concentration at 5 g/L in CgXII medium.
Fix biotin concentration at 0.2 mg/L in CgXII medium.
Fix protocatechuic acid (PCA) concentration at 30 mg/L in CgXII medium.
Fix IPTG concentration at 100 µM in CgXII medium.
Select high and low concentrations of media components for initial sensitivity screenings.
Use (NH4)2SO4 at 8-32 g/L as the standard nitrogen source.
Vary FeSO4 ∙ 7 H2O concentration from 4 to 16 mg/L.
Adjust MnSO4 ∙ H2O concentration between 4 and 16 mg/L.
Set ZnSO4 ∙ 7 H2O concentration from 0.4 to 1.6 mg/L.
Use CuSO4 ∙ 5 H2O at concentrations of 125-501 µg/L.
Incorporate NiCl2 ∙ 6 H2O in the range of 8-32 µg/L.
Include CoCl2 ∙ 6 H2O from 52 to 208 µg/L.
Add Na2MoO4 ∙ H2O at concentrations of 26-104 µg/L.
Use H3BO3 in the range of 20-80 µg/L.
Mix MgSO4 ∙ 7 H2O from 0.2 to 0.4 g/L.
Set CaCl2 ∙ 2 H2O concentration between 5.3 and 21.2 mg/L.
Prepare individual stock solutions for all investigated media components.
Avoid adding highly concentrated solutions that result in very low addition volumes, e.g., less than 1/100th of the final cultivation volume.
Dilute stock solutions as necessary to avoid impractical pipetting volumes, such as less than 10 μL.
Concentrate trace element solutions up to 1,000-fold with respect to their final standard concentration in the medium.
Prepare single colonies of the recombinant expression strain C. glutamicum pCGPhoDBs-GFP43 on agar plates (37 g/L BHI powder, 20 g/L agar, 25 mg/L kanamycin).
Incubate at 30 °C until appearance of single colonies.
Inoculate a shaker flask culture with colony material in 50 mL BHI medium with 25 mg/L kanamycin (500 mL baffled flask, 250 rpm, 25 mm shaking diameter, 30 °C).
Incubate overnight (approximately 16 h).
Combine one volume of resulting cell suspension with one volume of 500 g/L sterile glycerol solution.
Distribute in 2 mL aliquots in sterile cryopreservation vials.
Store at -80 °C.
Determine suitable gain values for biomass and GFP detection in preliminary experiments.
Determine suitable shaking frequency and filling volume to avoid oxygen limitation at higher biomass concentrations during later process stages.
Employ cultivation conditions with "Flowerplates", i.e., flower-shaped 48-well MTPs, shaking frequency of 1,200 rpm, and filling volume of 1,000 µL.
Use 10 g/L glucose as the main carbon source for the cultivations.
Check biomass concentrations at the end of cultivations to ensure no growth defects due to low amounts of secondary substrates.
Set Filterset 1 gain to 14 for biomass detection.
Set Filterset 2 gain to preset value for pH detection.
Set Filterset 3 gain to preset value for pO2 detection.
Set Filterset 4 gain to 80 for GFP detection.
Calculate the volume of Rest Stock containing fixed components for all wells based on experimentally determined precision and accuracy.
Adjust concentrations of Variation Stocks if necessary to accommodate minimal pipetting volumes (e.g., 10 µL).
Prepare Rest Stock accordingly.
Per cultivation well, calculate the volume of water to be added based on specified formulae.
List all volumes to be added per cultivation well in order: VH2O, VRestStock, Vi, VInok.
Seed culture using an automated liquid handling robot.
Ensure a sufficient runtime of sterile housing before media preparation.
Perform an initial excessive cleaning and washing of all pipetting tips and tubing.
Choose deep well plates with 12 columns for storage of variation stocks, allowing parallel dipping by eight pipetting tips to speed up media preparation.
Use 15 mL or 50 mL reagent tubes as reservoirs for stock solutions when only one tip can dip into them at a time.
Utilize 100 mL troughs for higher volume stock solutions like water and rest stock.
Provide sufficient total volume for each stock solution to account for waste volumes, height pipetting offsets, etc.
Insert a user prompt before the inoculation step, ensuring it is carried out immediately prior to seed culture procedure.
Prepare all stock solutions in a sterile manner and store them until use in appropriate containers such as sterile 15 mL and 50 mL test tubes.
Sterilize deep well plates with 70% ethanol.
Dry sterilized deep well plates in a laminar flow hood.
Inoculate 50 mL BHI medium containing kanamycin with one aliquot from the WCB.
Prepare fresh, vital inoculum from exponentially growing seed cultures.
Place necessary labware on the robotic worktable.
Pour stock solutions into corresponding labware.
Start the robotic workflow for media preparation.
Sample seed culture after approximately 2 hours.
Monitor growth by optical density (OD600) every hour.
Inoculate main cultures when seed culture reaches 3-4 OD600.
Place the seed culture on the liquid handler worktable.
Continue media preparation protocol.
Seal cultivation MTP after inoculation.
Place sealed cultivation MTP in the BioLector device.
Start pre-defined cultivation protocol.
Dispose remaining stock solutions according to biosafety regulations if necessary.
Seed culture from the robotic worktable.
Clean re-usable labware.
Start liquid handler decontamination protocol.
Stop the main culture after a 17 h runtime.
Transfer measurement data from BioLector MBR device to the connected computer using the provided software package.
Use the "Data Management → Transform Data" function of the BioLection software to convert raw data into an accessible spreadsheet format.
Copy GFP signal data for all cultivation wells from the timestamp closest to 17 h.
Identify and average the GFP signals from reference cultivation wells.
Normalize all remaining GFP signals by dividing them with the average reference signal.
Quantify GFP titer using additional methods if necessary.
Transfer cell suspensions from all cultivation wells into prelabeled reaction tubes.
Centrifuge the tubes for 10 min at maximum speed to obtain cell-free supernatant.
Transfer 200 µL of each cell-free supernatant into black 96-well MTP with transparent bottom.
Read GFP specific fluorescence at 488/520 nm using a microplate reader.
Normalize the GFP signal from all wells by dividing them with the average reference signal.
Determine the protein content of cell-free supernatants using standard protocols, e.g., Bradford or BCA assay.
Perform an SDS-Page visualization of cell-free supernatants following standard protocols to verify increased GFP secretion.
Choose an initial concentration range for media components.
Select a reference medium composition within chosen ranges.
Choose an appropriate design of experiments (DOE).
Perform 32 experiments using the "2IV11-6" design.
Estimate the effect of increasing one component's concentration on objectives.
Use remaining wells for multiple replicates with the reference medium.
Spread replicates equally over the plate to discover positional effects.
Calculate the mean value of the measured output from the reference experiments.
Normalize each measured output by dividing it by the mean value of the reference output.
Calculate main and combinatorial effects using appropriate statistics software.
Estimate polynomial coefficients using the mvregress function in MATLAB.
Identify relevant effects of various media components on the objective using a t-test.
Construct a Kriging model using the combined data from all iterations.
Investigate the model output by visualization using KriKit tools.
Check if the estimated optimal area was determined with sufficient accuracy.
If not, continue optimization.
Redo sensitivity analysis for the optimal medium composition after completing iterative optimization.
